result.summary: Independently re-derived verdict directly from lib/letflow/design/iss0276-dev-bootstrap-seed.md (not from CODE-DESIGNER's step-02 summary, which was read only to confirm what was asked). Verified each acceptance_criteria item: (1) all 3 of ISS-0276's ACs map to concrete design elements -- AC1 to design SS2 steps 1-4 (create_tenant/1 with idp_realm_id=bpm-default) plus SS8's explicit coverage table row; AC2 to SS2 steps 4-5 (provision_tenant_schema/1 + replay_migrations/1 actually provisioning the schema, not just inserting a row) plus SS8's row; AC3 to SS7 (README location) plus the task's own @moduledoc/@shortdoc, both named as required. (2) Idempotency (SS4) is explicit and unambiguous: on {:error, :duplicate_slug} from create_tenant/1, the task calls resolve_tenant_by_realm("bpm-default") and continues the provision/replay chain against the existing tenant_id if found, or Mix.raise/1 on a genuine slug collision (:not_found) -- no case left open for ELIXIR-DEV to invent. (3) LETFLOW_DEV_DB_CONFIRMED interaction (SS3) independently verified against the actual guard: read lib/letflow/repo.ex's init/2 in full (lines 16-45) -- confirms it raises unless config[:require_dev_db_confirmation] is falsy or LETFLOW_DEV_DB_CONFIRMED is set, and fires on repo connection, not repo module load; read config/dev.exs:49 -- confirms require_dev_db_confirmation: true is actually set there. The design's claim that Mix.Task.run("app.start") in the task's own step 1 triggers this guard before any task-specific code runs (so no duplicate check is needed in the new task) is consistent with both files -- verified directly, not accepted on the design doc's own account. (4) Documentation location named exactly: README.md 'Running it' section, after the existing LETFLOW_DEV_DB_CONFIRMED=1 mix ecto.setup / mix run --no-halt fenced block and before the curl health-check block -- read README.md lines 75-114 directly and confirmed this is precisely the existing structure (fenced block at lines 81-86, curl block starting line 100), so the design's insertion point is real and correctly located, not approximate. Plus the task's own @moduledoc/@shortdoc as the second, code-adjacent copy -- also named exactly (module Mix.Tasks.Letflow.Seed, file lib/mix/tasks/letflow.seed.ex). (5) No .ex function bodies or compilable implementation code anywhere in the design doc -- confirmed by reading the full document: only module/function signatures (@shortdoc, @spec run(args :: [String.t()]) :: :ok, def run(_args) with no body), a plain attrs-map literal (data shape, not code), and prose describing call sequence and branching logic in numbered steps. Cross-checked cited source claims against actual code: lib/letflow/identity.ex create_tenant/1 @spec (lines 582-583) and its {:error, :duplicate_slug} branch (lines 591-596) match; lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex confirms replay_migrations/2 with default migration_source \\ nil (line 303) and provision_tenant_schema/1 (line 229) match the design's arity claims; lib/mix/tasks/letflow.copy_identity_tables.ex confirms the cited Mix.Task.run("app.start") / Mix.shell().info / Mix.raise/1 style precedent is real, not fabricated. No gaps found; no TBD/deferral language on any load-bearing point -- SS6's two open questions (display_name literal choice, regression-test invocation strategy) are explicitly flagged as non-blocking and have no effect on any acceptance criterion, not left-open ambiguity on the design's core resolution points.
